title: Bodycam

anticheat.note: Added in the game's v0.9 update of 2026-11-13, as the developer's Steam announcement says. The launch stops at 'Failed to load the anti-cheat module' (highball-db#1200). On Windows Easy Anti-Cheat loads a kernel driver, which Wine can't run, and the runtime it ships for Proton on Linux has no macOS build.

provenance: Reported by phmuni (highball-db#121, 2026-09-18): rated 3, playable with workarounds, Apple M5 (base), macOS 27.0, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r3, Highball 0.9.23, about 15 minutes played through Highball including online matches. Renderer D3DMetal, added in a follow-up comment. Not run here. zn2m4swhkv-sys (highball-db#241, 2026-09-28): rated 3, playable with workarounds, Apple M2 24 GB MacBook Air, macOS 27, Highball 0.9.38, engine x64-crossover26.3-r12 (r10 and r12 ran best for them), D3DMetal, frame rate limit 120 (uncapped crashed), Windows 11, AVX advertised, a long list of audio DLL overrides tried against the audio problem. MichaelHackson (highball-db#1200, 2026-11-14), Apple M4, macOS 27.2.1, Highball 0.10.26, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28, D3DMetal, rated 1 of 5: 'Failed to load the anti-cheat module' from Easy Anti-Cheat since the game's v0.9 update of November 13, 2026, after it had played through Highball before; verifying the game files and repairing the environment didn't help.
notes: Since its v0.9 update of 2026-11-13 the game ships Easy Anti-Cheat, and the launch stops at 'Failed to load the anti-cheat module' (highball-db#1200), so it doesn't start on a Mac for now. What follows is from before that update. Unreal Engine 5 first-person shooter, Direct3D 12 only, and the report ran it on D3DMetal (from 0.9.26 Play picks that for Unreal 5 builds on its own). On a base M5 the one report gets about 40 to 50 fps on the training ground and around 30 fps online with every setting low, TSR at Quality, and the render resolution at half the display's native. Playable, but the reporter's own verdict is that a shooter at 30 to 40 fps is not the experience of better hardware. The game asks to install its Unreal prerequisites at every launch; agreeing to every prompt, including the ones labelled uninstall, lets it run (0.9.25 and later adopt runtimes a game installs, which may end the repeat prompts). A second report, on an M2 MacBook Air with the Wine 11 engine, averages about 23 fps with stretches of 30 to 45, and hits a problem the first did not: gunfire sets off an audio feedback loop and the frame rate sinks gradually after it. Their audio DLL overrides were an attempt against it, not a fix. Their later edit adds the settings that ran at 800p: AMD upscaling at Quality, frame generation on, the in-game limit at 30 and global illumination on High, so the non-TSR upscaler crash seen on the M5 with engine r3 did not happen there. Lobbies held steady, matches with bots were heavier with pop-in at the start, and an 8BitDo SN30 Pro controller made turning sluggish where a mouse played better.

knownIssues.symptom: 'Failed to load the anti-cheat module' at launch since the v0.9 update of 2026-11-13, and the game never reaches its menu (M4, D3DMetal, Wine 10 r28, highball-db#1200)
knownIssues.cause: Easy Anti-Cheat, added in that update, can't load under Wine on macOS

knownIssues.symptom: Asks to install UE prerequisites at every launch
knownIssues.cause: the game's prerequisite check does not see the runtimes as installed in the environment
knownIssues.fix: Agree to every prompt, including the ones labelled uninstall, and it runs; on 0.9.25 or later the environment adopts installed runtimes, which may stop the repeat prompts

knownIssues.symptom: Choosing any upscaler other than TSR or Off crashes the game, and afterwards it runs at 5 to 8 fps with the in-game menus locked, even after deleting the user config in AppData\Local
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed; the non-TSR upscalers (reported on M5, macOS 27, engine r3) leave a broken state the config wipe alone does not clear; an M2 Air on the Wine 11 engine r12 ran AMD upscaling at Quality without it (highball-db#241)
knownIssues.fix: Stay on TSR or Off. If it has already happened, uninstall the game, clear its AppData\Local files, and reinstall; the reporter says it can come back if those settings are changed again

knownIssues.symptom: Gunfire sets off an audio feedback loop and the frame rate sinks gradually after it (reported on an M2 Air, Wine 11 engine r12, D3DMetal).
knownIssues.fix: none known. Uncapped frame rate crashed for that player, a 120 cap held.
